facts.heading: Anxiety worsening in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this anxiety worsened in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: New role at school started
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school, where she has taught for 11 years.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school. I've taught here for 11 years

facts.heading: Promoted to deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was asked to step up when the previous deputy left.
facts.evidence: And then had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah worries that people picked the wrong person for her new role.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person.

facts.heading: Fear of being exposed
facts.content: Hannah fears that someone will eventually notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Sunday evening anxiety symptoms
facts.content: On Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest gets tight, and she starts rehearsing Monday's meetings in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing worst-case scenarios
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question someone might ask and what she would say.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say then

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah imagines what people would think of her if she got something wrong.
facts.evidence: what they would think of me if I got it wrong

facts.heading: Email rewriting due to fear
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governor four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governor's four times.

facts.heading: Fear of governor's judgment
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding a policy change.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves's positive treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah, and he was delighted with her in September.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind. He talked me in September. He was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable.
facts.evidence: About being capable as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like an imposter
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: Pretending to be what? Somebody who knows what she's doing.

facts.heading: Feeling like child in coat
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares herself to her mother and wonders if her mother would have done things better.
facts.evidence: Everything they do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive nature
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface, saying Hannah worries too much.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feeling unheard by mother
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss when her mother tells her to stop worrying.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four every morning

facts.heading: Morning thoughts cause distress
facts.content: Hannah spends time going through her to-do list when she wakes at four.
facts.evidence: Then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list

facts.heading: Worries include timetable changes
facts.content: Hannah's worries include timetable changes, offset prep, a parent complaint, and a child she is worried about.
facts.evidence: Everything, timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about

facts.heading: Waking pattern started in term
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Consumes five to six coffees
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons

facts.evidence: My heart goes fast.
